claim: Netcast (MIT): measured OPTICAL energy per MAC at the time-integrating receiver for MNIST at 98.8% accuracy
quote: We demonstrate operation in a photon-starved environment with 40 aJ/multiply of optical energy for 98.8% accurate image recognition and <1 photon/multiply using single photon detectors.
notes: Optical energy only, computed from integrated charge (Supp. Sec. 'Calculation of Receiver Noise'). EXCLUDES laser wall-plug, the server-side smart transceiver that modulates the weights (48 MZMs, 50 Gb/s each), client input modulator/DAC, integrator electronics and ADC. Not a system number.

claim: Netcast: MACs accumulated on the time-integrating receiver per readout (integration window) in the main experiments
locator: Supplementary Materials, section 'Calculation of Receiver Noise' (time integrating receiver paragraph)
quote: This energy is then divided by the number of MACs performed per integration window, which in the main text is M = 100.
notes: ADC conversions per MAC = 1/M = 0.01 (DERIVED). Each wavelength channel has its own photodiode + integrator; the photodetector does the accumulate in charge.

claim: Netcast: measured computational precision of optical multiplications (sigma_rms = 0.005)
quote: has a standard deviation of σrms = 0.005 or ≈ 8-bit accuracy.
notes: Scalar-scalar multiplications (10,000 samples), not a full dot-product at 40 aJ/MAC; precision at the lowest-energy operating point is lower (accuracy vs energy curve Fig. 4).

claim: Netcast: client electrical energy per MAC with N = M = 100 using conventional components (Table I: modulator ~1 pJ, DAC ~1 pJ, ADC ~1 pJ, integrator ~1 fJ, amortised)
locator: Main text, section 'Energy efficiency' and Table I
quote: Assuming near-term values of N = M = 100, client energy consumption can reach ≈10 fJ/MAC, which is three orders of magnitude lower than possible in existing digital CMOS.
notes: Component literature values, not measured. EXCLUDES the weight-broadcasting server (weights are modulated per MAC by the smart transceiver; amortised only across clients sharing the broadcast), lasers, memory. Client-side accounting only.

claim: Netcast: operating (readout) rate of the deployed-fibre demonstration
quote: Because of loss along the fiber the system is operated at a speed of 1kHz.
notes: Integrator reset time 10 us (Supp.). Off-the-shelf integrator IC with default 10 pF capacitance. The 3 THz optical bandwidth is not the electrical throughput. Speed tier: slow proof of principle.

claim: Netcast: shot-noise-limited operation with superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors, <1 photon per MAC
locator: Main text, section 'Receiver sensitivity' (Fig. 5); Supp. Fig. 4 (SNSPD in 0.8 K cryostat)
quote: allows the receiver to operate with high accuracy with < 1 photon per MAC (0.1 aJ/MAC).
notes: Requires SNSPDs in a 0.8 K cryostat, clocked at 30 kHz (Supp.). Cryocooler energy not counted. Not a room-temperature system.

claim: Photoelectric multiplication (homodyne detection + charge integration) accelerator: simulated standard quantum limit of optical energy per MAC
quote: This bound, which can be as low as 50 zJ/MAC, suggests performance below the thermodynamic (Landauer) limit for digital irreversible computation is theoretically possible in this device.
notes: Simulation; shot-noise bound on optical energy only. Paper: electronics can be slow 'since only the integrated charge is measured'. Physics-limit territory overlaps R8.

claim: Free-space ONN (OLED + SLM, detector integrates the dot product): detected optical energy per scalar multiplication at ~90% MNIST
quote: ∼90% accuracy using ∼0.64 photons (∼2.4 × 10−19 J of optical energy) per weight multiplication.
notes: arXiv v1 numbers; Nat Commun 13:123 (2022) version states 3.1 / 0.66 photons. 99% accuracy needs ~3.2 photons. Excludes OLED, SLM, detector electronics: optical-core only.

claim: Free-space ONN: <1 photon per multiplication demonstrated at a rate of at least 10 MHz (detector integration ~100 ns)
quote: This shows that matrix-vector multiplications can be performed with <1 photon per multiplication at a rate of at least 10 MHz
notes: Vector length ~0.5 million (711 x 711 pixels); one detector integrates the whole dot product, i.e. 1 readout per ~5e5 multiplications.

claim: Single-photon-detector (SPD) neural network: detection event itself is the (binary stochastic) activation; optical energy per MAC at 98% MNIST
quote: the optical energy used to perform the classification corresponds to just 0.038 photons per multiply–accumulate (MAC) operation.
notes: Hidden-layer activations are SPD clicks (conversion = activation); output layer uses a conventional high-SNR photodetector array. Single hidden layer (784-N-10). SPD electronics, light source and control excluded.

claim: TFLN integrated photonic tensor core (2 TFLN MZMs + III-V laser + charge-integration balanced photoreceiver): measured computational speed
quote: The two vectors were modulated separately by two modulators at a modulation rate of 60 Gbaud, enabling a computational speed of 120 GOPS, and a weight update speed of 60 GHz.
notes: Time-division MAC: product formed optically by two cascaded modulators, accumulated as charge on the integrator. Both operands are streamed from an AWG (see R7-017 for the DAC implication).

claim: TFLN tensor core: measured dot-product precision (std 0.03 on 131,072-element vectors)
quote: Compared with the expected dot product result, the error of the measured one has a standard deviation of 0.03 (6.04 bits)
notes: 3780 dot products of 131,072-element random vectors.

claim: TFLN tensor core: fan-in accumulated on one charge-integration photoreceiver before a single ADC read
quote: Our processor can handle a fan-in size of 131,072–significantly surpassing the capacity of previously reported IPTCs by four orders of magnitude
notes: ADC sampling rate need only be fs/n (paper). ADC conversions per MAC = 1/131072 = 7.6e-6 (DERIVED). Fan-in was capped by the AWG memory, not the integrator.

claim: TFLN tensor core: balanced detection on the integrator gives signed (add and subtract) accumulation
quote: This means that the proposed photoreceiver can perform add and subtract operations in the matrix-vector multiplication.
notes: PD1/PD2 in balanced configuration on one integrator; signed weights without a second optical pass.

claim: TFLN tensor core: projected energy efficiency for a 64-wavelength x 64-core version, including laser, DACs, charge-integration receivers, CMOS switches and comparators
quote: we can achieve a computational speed of 491 TOPS and an energy efficiency of 6.5 fJ/OP ( i.e ., 153 TOPS/W), factoring in a modulation speed of 60 Gbaud/s, including the energy consumption of the laser, DACs, charge-integration photoreceivers
notes: No measured energy for the built device. Projection assumes K = m = 64 (comb + 64-ch WDM, not built). Memory/weight fetch not listed as included.

claim: TFLN tensor core: MNIST accuracy of the 4-layer MLP trained in situ vs CPU
quote: shows an accuracy of 91.8 % for the generated predictions, in contrast to 92% for the numerical results calculated on a CPU.
notes: 500 test images.

claim: DERIVED: a TDM dot-product engine that streams BOTH operands needs 2 DAC samples per MAC; at the R3 DAC energy (0.5-1 pJ per operation, R3-038) that is 1-2 pJ/MAC unless operands are fanned out/reused
quote: The two vectors were modulated separately by two modulators at a modulation rate of 60 Gbaud
notes: DERIVED: 2 samples/MAC x 0.5-1 pJ/sample (R3-038) = 1-2 pJ/MAC. The ADC is amortised 131,072x but the DAC burden moves to 2 per MAC. The authors' 6.5 fJ/OP projection relies on WDM/core fan-out (K = m = 64) to amortise DACs. Conversion count is shifted, not removed.

claim: Coherent VCSEL ONN (homodyne photoelectric multiplication + time integration): reported 'full-system' energy per OP
locator: Main text, 'System performance - Energy efficiency'; Supplementary Table I
quote: Thereby the full-system energy efficiency including both electronic and optical consumption is 7 fJ/OP (Supplementary Table I)
notes: Component budget: VCSEL bias measured; ADC ~1 pJ/use, TIA ~1 pJ/use, integrator ~1 fJ/use, DAC ~0.5 pJ/use, memory ~100 fJ/access are LITERATURE values amortised over i = 784 time steps and j = 81 fan-out. 1 MAC = 2 OP (Supp. Table I note 2). Not a wall-plug measurement. See R7-025.

claim: VCSEL ONN: 'optical' energy efficiency computed from measured VCSEL bias (Pb ~400 uW) at the maximum clock R = 1 GS/s and fan-out j = 81
quote: The maximum clock rate of the system is R=1 GS/s. With a fanout factor j = 9×9, the optical energy efficiency is (Pb + Pinj + Pm )/(2jR)=2.5 fJ/OP, dominated by the laser power.
notes: Counts only the input ('axon') VCSEL; each weight VCSEL is biased too and serves one output channel (k = 1 in the MNIST demo). MNIST data were taken at 100 MS/s, not 1 GS/s.

claim: VCSEL ONN: ADC energy per use assumed ~1 pJ and amortised over i = 28 x 28 integrated time steps
quote: ADC7 (EADC ) ∼ 1 pJ/use [5] i=28×28 0.5 fJ
notes: ADC conversions per MAC = 1/784 (DERIVED, one read per image-length integration). Energy per use is a literature citation, not measured.

claim: VCSEL ONN: memory access assumed ~100 fJ/access, amortised over the j = 81 spatial fan-out
locator: Supplementary Table I, Memory access row
quote: Memory access9 (EMEM ) ∼ 100 fJ/access j=9×9 0.6 fJ
notes: 100 fJ/access is SRAM-class; no HBM/DRAM weight streaming term (R3-078: 11.68 pJ/bit measured HBM). For an LLM this row would dominate.

claim: VCSEL ONN: MNIST accuracy of a 3-layer (784-100-10-10) network on hardware
quote: we obtain an accuracy of (93.1 ± 2)%, which is 98 % of the model’s accuracy in simulation (95.1%).
notes: Layers are cascaded through digital serialization of integrated values, not optically. 158.8 million operations over 1000 images.

claim: VCSEL ONN: measured homodyne compute precision
quote: reveals a computing accuracy of 98% (∼6 bits of precision), limited mainly by the phase instability of the setup

claim: VCSEL ONN: clock rate actually used for the MNIST data (AWG-limited, five VCSELs per acquisition)
quote: the data is taken with multiple acquisitions (five VCSELs per acquisition) at the clock rate of 100 MS/s, although the VCSEL bandwidth allows homodyne interference at > 1 GS/s

claim: DERIVED: VCSEL ONN at batch 1 (weight fan-out k = 1): per-OP cost of the weight side using the paper's own Table I unit values
locator: Main text, paragraph after the 7 fJ/OP statement
quote: which reduces the energy for weighing to the same order of the input encoding
notes: DERIVED: weight VCSEL bias 400 fJ/symbol / 2 OP = 200 fJ/OP; weight DAC 0.5 pJ/use / 2 = 250 fJ/OP; weight memory 100 fJ/access / 2 = 50 fJ/OP; + 7 fJ/OP table total = ~507 fJ/OP. Assumes (inferred, not stated) that Table I's DAC/memory/laser rows amortise only the input side by j; the paper says weight fan-out k (batch) is needed to bring weighting to the input-encoding order. Treat as an upper-bound sensitivity, not a finding.

claim: TeMPO time-multiplexed photonic tensor core (capacitive temporal integration of photocurrent): architecture-level energy efficiency
quote: We achieve a 368.6 TOPS peak performance, 22.3 TOPS/W energy efficiency, and 1.2 TOPS/mm2 compute density, pushing the Pareto frontier in edge AI hardware.
notes: Architecture evaluation; one slow-light MZM was fabricated at AIM Photonics MPW and measured, the system was not built. Temporal integration is 'one of the key mechanisms ... to significantly relieve the ADC power bottleneck'; DAC dominates the remaining power (paper Fig. 16-18).

claim: Waveguide-multiplexed MVM: a multiport Ge photodetector sums intensities of 16 waveguides (detector-side accumulation, single wavelength); measured bandwidth
quote: A 16-port Ge PD with a 3 dB bandwidth of 11.8 GHz at a bias voltage of -3 V is demonstrated, and it can be further scaled up to handle 250 ports while maintaining a 6.1 GHz operation bandwidth.
notes: Fabricated by AMF (foundry Ge-on-Si). One PD read per 16 summed products -> ADC conversions per MAC = 1/16 (DERIVED). No energy per MAC reported.

claim: Multiport PD: projected scaling to 250 input ports at 6.1 GHz
quote: it can be further scaled up to handle 250 ports while maintaining a 6.1 GHz operation bandwidth.
notes: Scaling statement, not a fabricated 250-port device.

claim: Multiport PD 4x4 circuit: Iris 3-layer network accuracy with on-chip MVMs
quote: A 4 × 4 circuit fabricated on a Si-on-insulator (SOI) platform is used to perform MVMs in a 3-layer neural network designed for classifying Iris flowers, achieving a classification accuracy of 93.3%.
notes: Heater MZIs as weights (~1.3 mW/pi), four 4-port PDs; nonlinearity and inter-layer handling electronic.

claim: Single-shot free-space ONN: projected energy per MAC of an optimised CMOS-compatible version, including sources, detectors, DAC, ADC, SLM, TIA and electronic nonlinearity
quote: The energy of our single-shot ONN, on the other hand, is on the order of ∼10 fJ/MAC, including a source wall-plug efficiency of 10% [33,53], PD responsivity of 0.2 A/W
notes: Theoretical, K = 1000 layer with static weights on the SLM. Same paper: weights that do not fit must be fetched from memory, 'subjecting them to the same memory wall' (R7-031).

claim: Single-shot ONN authors: accelerators with limited scalability must fetch matrices from memory over multiple time steps -> same memory wall as digital
quote: matrices that do not fit onto the hardware must be fetched from memory over multiple time steps, subjecting them to the same ‘memory wall’ that currently bottlenecks digital electronics.
notes: Supports R3's decode finding: conversion-as-compute does not touch the HBM weight-streaming term.

claim: Single-chip end-to-end photonic deep network (PDNN): classification time
quote: the non-linear activation function is realized opto-electronically, allowing a classification time of under 570 ps
notes: Main text paywalled. arXiv v1 (2106.11747) bases end-to-end speed on component bandwidths (ring modulator and SiGe PD >30 GHz), not on a stated timing measurement -> classed STUDY-ASSUMED. 3 layers (4x12-input, 3x4-input, 2x3-input neurons). No energy per classification reported in the accessible text.

claim: PDNN: measured 2-class and 4-class handwritten-letter accuracy
quote: Two-class and four-class classification of handwritten letters with accuracies higher than 93.8% and 89.8%, respectively, is demonstrated.
notes: arXiv v1 reports 93.7% / 90.3%; reference Keras CNN 96%. Clock-less: no ADC/DAC between layers.

claim: PDNN neuron: photocurrents of parallel SiGe photodiodes are summed, converted by an OFF-CHIP TIA which drives an on-chip microring modulator (ReLU); number of off-chip TIAs
quote: Seven off-chip TIAs are used to drive the on-chip modulators.
notes: So the demonstrated O-E-O neuron removes ADC/DAC/SRAM between layers but NOT the TIA; TIA power is not reported. Weights set by PIN current-controlled attenuators (forward-biased, static power).

claim: PDNN: supply-light laser power feeding every neuron's modulator (per-neuron regeneration, cascadability by fresh supply light)
quote: Laser 2 emits 2.5 mW at 1559.93 nm.
notes: Image-forming laser was separately amplified to ~63 mW by an EDFA; ~42 dB path loss from collimator to each pixel (arXiv v1 Methods). Chip in AMF 180 nm SOI.

claim: PDNN chip foundry process (active: SiGe PDs, PIN attenuators, PN microring modulators)
quote: The microphotograph of the photonic chip implemented in the AMF 180 nm SOI process.
notes: Foundry-available active process; not buildable on a passive+heater run.

claim: FICONN nonlinear optical function unit (NOFU): photodiode directly drives a pn microring modulator ('receiverless', no amplifier); energy per nonlinear operation
quote: As each NOFU performs the equivalent of two multiplications in digital electronics, over a carrier lifetime of ∼1 ns this corresponds to an energy consumption of 30 fJ per nonlinear operation (NLOP).
notes: Author estimate from MEASURED 75 uA photocurrent needed for one-linewidth detuning plus an assumed ~1 ns carrier lifetime. Electrical side only; excludes the tapped optical power and the heater that aligns the ring.

claim: FICONN: same NOFU with a conventional high-speed TIA inserted
quote: For our device, incorporating such an amplifier would have increased the power consumption by two orders of magnitude to about 3 pJ/NLOP.
notes: Quantifies what removing the receiver saves at the activation: ~100x.

claim: DERIVED: optical power tapped to the NOFU photodiode to detune the ring by a linewidth, times the ~1 ns carrier lifetime
quote: Assuming a photodiode responsivity of ∼ 1 A/W, we find that about 75 µW is sufficient to detune the NOFU
notes: DERIVED: 75e-6 W x 1e-9 s = 75 fJ of optical energy removed from the signal per activation, in addition to the 30 fJ electrical figure. Responsivity 1 A/W is an assumption of the authors.

claim: FICONN (3 coherent matrix layers, 2 NOFU layers, N = 6 modes): estimated inference latency from the fabricated layout
quote: which we estimate from the PIC subsystems (as described in the SI) as 3τCMXU + 2τNOFU + τTX to U1 + τU3 to RX + τU-turn ≈ 435 ps.
notes: Time-of-flight estimate, not a measured latency. Whole-chip on-chip energy upper bound 9.8 pJ/OP is dominated by thermal phase shifters (R3-055).

claim: FICONN: vowel classification accuracy after in-situ training
quote: Our system achieves over 96% accuracy on the training set, and over 92% accuracy on the test set
notes: Layers cascaded optically through NOFUs: no ADC/DAC between layers.

claim: FICONN (incl. receiverless NOFU with Ge PD + pn microring) fabricated in a commercial foundry process
quote: The photonic integrated circuit (PIC) was fabricated in a commercial silicon photonics process by Elenion Technologies.
notes: Active process with Ge photodiodes and carrier-based ring modulators.

claim: Silicon photonic modulator neuron: balanced photodetector wired directly to a microring modulator (O-E-O, no amplifier), fabricated in a conventional silicon photonic process line
quote: The neuron consists of a balanced photodetector directly connected to a microring (MRR) modulator.
notes: Balanced PD = signed fan-in (excitatory/inhibitory). Injection-mode modulation used.

claim: Modulator neuron: optical-to-optical small-signal gain on chip (fibre-to-fibre measured 2.16e-2; 18 dB coupling loss removed)
quote: Removing the coupling loss results in an on-chip gain estimate of 1.36.
notes: Pump held 'artificially low'; gain scales with pump power. Gain >1 is the cascadability condition. Cascadability demonstrated as an autapse (one neuron feeding itself), not a multi-layer network.

claim: NTT femtofarad O-E-O 'transistor' (PhC photodiode + PhC electro-absorption modulator, no amplifier), normally-off at 10 Gbit/s: total energy per bit
unit: fJ/bit (1.6 optical PD + 3.2 electrical + 16.7 optical EOM)
quote: Eopt_PD = 1.6 fJ/bit Eelect = 3.2 fJ/bit for ηpd = 1 A/W and Vbias = 2 V Eopt_EOM = 16.7 ± 3.8 fJ/bit for 10 Gbit/s Etotal = 21.5 ± 3.8 fJ/bit
notes: Author accounting of measured quantities. Output/transmitted energy 0.95 fJ/bit (conversion efficiency 0.6 -> no gain in this mode). InP/InGaAs(P) photonic-crystal membrane, 2 fF: not a silicon foundry process. Digital switching, not an analog activation.

claim: NTT O-E-O transistor, normally-on at 2.5 Gbit/s: total energy per bit with optical conversion gain 2.3
quote: Normally-on condition operating at a bit rate of 2.5 Gbit/s Eopt_PD = 6.4 fJ/bit Eelect = 12.8 fJ/bit for ηpd = 1 A/W and Vbias = 2 V
notes: Etotal = 60.1 +/- 5.7 fJ/bit, eta_conv = 2.3 +/- 0.3 (same table). Gain regime costs ~3x the energy and 4x the speed.

claim: NTT O-E-O transistor: optical signal gain from peak-power measurement (32 uW in)
quote: and an optical gain of 1.8 − 2.4 is estimated by comparison with the input peak power of 32 µW.
notes: Cascadable optical repeater function demonstrated in the main text (abstract).

claim: NTT amplifier-free resistor-loaded PhC photoreceiver (O-E conversion): total energy per bit
quote: This ensures that our receiver has a similar EBP performance to conventional receivers but has a remarkably low total energy consumption of only 4.8 fJ/bit.
notes: Receiverless O-E: compare the R3 TIA assumption of 2.4 pJ per sample (R3-062), ~500x more.

claim: NTT PhC electro-optic modulator (E-O conversion): energy per bit at 40 Gbit/s
locator: Supplementary Information, section 3 'Energy consumption for single PhC-EOM'
quote: Consequently, we conclude that the total energy consumption of a single PhC-EOM is only 42 aJ/bit for a 40 Gbit/s modulation.
notes: Charging ~40 aJ/bit + external supply ~2 aJ/bit.

claim: NTT O-E-O transistor: 3 dB bandwidth in the normally-off mode
quote: the normally-off operation exhibits f3dB = 3.3 GHz, a 10-Gbit/s eye diagram, and an optical conversion efficiency of 0.6.
notes: Normally-on (gain) mode limited to 0.9-2.0 GHz.

claim: Reprogrammable electro-optic activation (PD + gain circuit + modulator) design study: assumed optical-to-electrical circuit power
quote: Optical-to-electrical circuit power consumption 100 mW
notes: DERIVED: 100 mW / 10 GHz = 10 pJ per activation. Shows why amplified O-E-O activations do not save energy; receiverless designs (R7-037, R7-045) are 2-3 orders lower.

claim: EO-activation ONN design study: per-layer efficiency falling with N (2.5 pJ/MAC at N=4 to 100 fJ/MAC at N=100), assuming zero phase-shifter power
locator: Table II, per-layer figures of merit
quote: Efficiency ∗ N 2.5 pJ/MAC 1 pJ/MAC 100 fJ/MAC ∗ Assuming no power consumption in the interferometer mesh phase shifters
notes: Activation cost amortised 1/N.

claim: RTD-photodetector + VCSEL O/E/O spiking neuron (no ADC/DAC): measured spike duration
quote: We demonstrate a well defined excitability threshold, above which this neuron produces ∼100 ns optical spiking responses with characteristic neural-like refractory period.
notes: No measured energy per spike in the text; nanoscale projection not quantified in energy. Fan-in used for in-device coincidence detection (AND) and XOR (abstract); not a multi-layer network.

claim: Integrated photonic neural network trained end-to-end with on-chip backpropagation; all linear and nonlinear computations on one photonic chip
quote: In two nonlinear data classification tasks, chip performance matches that of the reference digital model in accuracy (over 90%) and robustness
notes: Main text paywalled: activation energy/latency not accessible. The 2023 arXiv precursor (2307.10179) uses photodiodes driving a microdisk modulator through an amplifier for the activation.

claim: TFLN chi(2) nonlinear splitter (SHG + degenerate OPA): measured 3 dB all-optical switching energy (through / drop port)
quote: The 3 dB switching energies at the through port and the drop port are 80 fJ and 20 fJ, respectively.
notes: Optical pulse energy only; needs 46-fs pulses at 2.09 um from a synchronously pumped OPO (table-top mode-locked source; wall-plug not counted). Not cascaded.

claim: TFLN chi(2) switch: switching time
quote: We achieve non-resonant all-optical switching with ultra-low energies down to tens of femtojoules, a near instantaneous switching time of 18 fs

claim: TFLN chi(2) switch: simulated switching energy for a 70-mm-long waveguide
quote: yields a 2 dB switching contrast at a switching energy of 800 aJ.
notes: Simulation.

claim: All-optical ReLU in periodically poled TFLN nanowaveguide: energy per activation (50% transmission change)
quote: In this case, our device has an energy per activation of ∼ 16 fJ. The bias pulse energy is not included since it is not dissipated and can be reused.
notes: Bias pulse excluded by convention; source is a Yb mode-locked laser + OPO (75-fs pulses, 250 MHz). Time per activation ~75 fs. Deep-learning performance shown in simulation only; no on-chip cascade.

claim: InGaAsP photonic-crystal nanocavity all-optical switch: switching energy (3 dB / 10 dB contrast)
quote: Switching energies with a contrast of 3 and 10 dB of 0.42 and 0.66 fJ, respectively, have been obtained
notes: Carrier nonlinearity, recovery within a few tens of ps. Main text paywalled (abstract only). III-V platform.

claim: All-optical spiking neuron with phase-change (GST) cell on a ring: firing threshold energy
quote: In this specific device/example an output pulse is generated if the switching power exceeds 430 pJ
notes: Single-layer network: 4 neurons, 60 synapses. PCM must be reset between events.

claim: PCM spiking neuron: maximum pulse energy used to switch the PCM cell
quote: the maximum pulse energy used to switch the PCM-cell in this experiment was 710 pJ employing optical pulses of 200 ns width.
notes: Weights set with similar energies (paper).

claim: Ge-Si photodiode used as an all-optical activation (absorption + free-carrier absorption) with built-in monitoring photocurrent: activation threshold
quote: The threshold of the nonlinear activation is about 1.1 mW.
notes: Standard Group-IV process element: the detector's own absorption nonlinearity is the activation and its photocurrent is the monitor (conversion doubles as compute + telemetry).

claim: Ge-Si photodiode activation: insertion loss of the all-optical neuron (output 0-1.6 mW)
quote: The actual output optical power of the AONU is between 0 and 1.6 mW under different input optical power, with the optical loss being estimated to be 6.2 dB.
notes: Loss <1 gain -> not self-cascadable without amplification (paper: neuron output is often weaker than its input).

claim: Ge-Si photodiode ONN: calculated energy per operation of the demonstrated system
quote: The consumed energy is calculated to be ~0.27 pJ per operation in our system
notes: Calculation in Supp. Note 10 (not read); assumes 20 GHz detection bandwidth.

claim: Ge-Si photodiode ONN: layers demonstrated (split over three chips linked by fibre arrays)
quote: Although the three-layer network can be built on one chip with the same fabrication process, we split it into three chips and connect them using optical fiber arrays
notes: Each layer 4 neurons, 16 MZIs, 4 nonlinear units.

claim: DERIVED: Ge-Si PD activation threshold energy per symbol at the paper's 20 GHz detection bandwidth
quote: the FLOPS is calculated to be 1.92 × 10 12 operations per second with a 20 GHz detection bandwidth.
notes: DERIVED: 1.1e-3 W / 20e9 s^-1 = 55 fJ per activation at threshold (R7-062). Laser wall-plug excluded.

claim: InP SOA cross-connect DNN: SOA used as the weighting (gain) element; drive power per SOA
quote: for every multiplication we assign a gain to an SOA via an average injected current of 35 mA, corresponding to a power consumption of 42 mW/SOA and a total power consumption of 2.7 W
notes: Nonlinearity was implemented in software. SOA gives optical gain (cascadable) but at pJ-class energy.

claim: InP SOA DNN: energy per operation at 10 GS/s
quote: the energy consumption is of order of 4.2 pJ/operation, which is of the same order as state-of-the-art electronics [14].
notes: Author estimate from measured SOA drive power and 10 GS/s.

claim: InP SOA DNN: 3-layer Iris accuracy and the dominant error source
quote: A comprehensive analysis of the error evolution in our system reveals that the electrical/optical conversions dominate the error contribution
notes: Prediction accuracy 85.8% vs 95% on a computer (abstract). Conversions cost accuracy as well as energy.

claim: WSe2 split-gate photodiode array as a neural network: photodiodes in short-circuit (photovoltaic) mode, weights = gate-set responsivity; classification latency
quote: In Fig. 5 we plot the electric output pulses, demonstrating the correct pattern classification within ~50 ns.
notes: 27 detectors (3x3 pixels x 3 subpixels). Throughput 20 Mbins/s limited by 20 MHz amplifiers. Activation off-chip. Nature 579, 62 (2020) is the published version.

claim: WSe2 array: where the weights are held
quote: In our present implementation the weights of the ANN are stored in an external memory and supplied to each detector via cabling.
notes: Volatile: gate voltages held by DACs. Floating-gate variant shown only as a single device (Supp. Fig. S4).

claim: Electrostatically doped (dual-gate) silicon p-i-n photodiodes with programmable responsivity: in-sensor convolution array size
quote: With a 3 × 3 network of the electrostatically doped photodiodes, we demonstrate in-sensor image processing using seven different convolutional filters electrically programmed into the photodiode network.
notes: CMOS-compatible silicon; thousands fabricated at wafer scale. Main text paywalled (abstract + supplement read). No energy per MAC in accessible text.

claim: Dual-gate Si photodiode: measured rise/fall time (TIA-limited)
quote: Rise and fall times of a pulse in this VTIA, measured between 10% and 90% of the full pulse amplitude, are 3 ns and 12 ns.
notes: Limited by the TIA module (1.5 kOhm, >=1 pF), not only the diode.

claim: Ferroelectric (PZT) photovoltaic photosensor: non-volatile responsivity levels per potentiation/depression sweep
quote: Notably, each LTD or LTP process contains 25 different R levels, confirming the accessibility to multiple photoresponsive states.
notes: Signed weight in one device (polarization sign). Cycle-to-cycle variation ~3%.

claim: Ferroelectric photosensor: retention of programmed responsivity
quote: the polarization-controlled photoresponsive states are stable with a rather long retention time of ≥24 h
notes: Domain states stable up to 18 days (PFM, same paper).

claim: Ferroelectric photosensor: write endurance
quote: photocurrents and associated remanent polarizations change only slightly after switching for 10^6 cycles
notes: 1e6 writes rules out per-token weight re-tiling (compare R3-012).

claim: Ferroelectric photosensor network: 'zero energy consumption for inference' is prospected, not measured; operates only under 365 nm UV
quote: the ultralow latency and zero energy consumption for inference are prospected for the FE-PS-NET
notes: Self-powered photovoltaic mode: light supplies the signal energy; readout current measurement, ADC and weight writes are outside the 'zero'. 3x3 array. 365 nm matches PZT bandgap (~3.6 eV): not usable at telecom wavelengths.

claim: Silicon photodiode + RRAM cell: self-powered, non-volatile programmable photo-responsivity; weight range from the shunt formula (R0 = 1 kOhm, R = 1-100 kOhm)
quote: Taking R 0 as 1 kΩ, when R is changed from 1 kΩ to 100 kΩ, the weight ranges from 0.0099 to 0.5.
notes: Formula range; measured responsivity tuning shown for 1-30 kOhm. 3x3 array demonstrated. No energy per MAC measured.

claim: MoS2 photodetector with programmable spectral responsivity (in-sensor spectral dot product): estimated device power
quote: The power consumption of the device presented below is estimated to be on the order of 10 nW
notes: Leakage-current estimate; excludes readout. 3 wavelength-selective segments.

claim: MANTIS near-sensor imager SoC: charge-domain MAC (switched-capacitor amplifiers + charge sharing in the SAR-ADC capacitive DAC); peak accelerator efficiency
quote: MANTIS achieves peak EEs normalized to 1b operations of 4.6 and 84.1 TOPS/W at the accelerator and SoC levels
notes: Table assigns 84.09 TOPS/W / 11.9 fJ/op to the ACCELERATOR (analog memory, SC amplifiers, SAR ADCs, drivers) and 4.57 TOPS/W to the SoC; the abstract's word order is inverted (negative finding). 4b weights x analog pixel inputs, normalised to 1b ops. Feature-map RMSE 3-11.3% (abstract). 0.11 um CMOS.

claim: MANTIS: peak SoC-level efficiency incl. imager analog macro, Cortex-M4 CPU, controller and SRAM
notes: Best column; Energy/OP (SoC) 0.22 pJ/op in the same column. Measured system-level charge-domain photodiode->MAC figure (normalised to 1b).

claim: MANTIS: SoC power at 29 fps and share taken by digital
quote: Power is dominated by the digital part, which represents 78% of the 335.6-µW SoC power
notes: After moving MACs into the charge domain, digital control/CPU/DMA dominate: the conversion-as-compute saving is capped by everything else.

claim: In-sensor photocurrent computing (review in MANTIS): weight resolution typically binary/ternary and limited by fixed-pattern noise
quote: in-sensor processing is often limited to low-complexity tasks as it relies on binary (1b) or ternary (1.5b) weights, and on raw [1], [2], [3] or amplified [9] photocurrents subject to significant fixed-pattern noise
notes: Precision ceiling for using the photodiode itself as the multiplier.

claim: Memristor binarized neural network (32,768 memristors) powered DIRECTLY by a miniature wide-bandgap solar cell with no interface/regulation circuitry
quote: we demonstrate the resilience of our binarized neural network by directly connecting the power supply pads of our circuit to the solar cell, without any interface circuitry.
notes: Halogen lamp illumination expressed as 'equivalent suns'. AlGaAs/GaInP cell, Voc 1.23 V at 8 suns matched to 1.2 V CMOS.

claim: Solar-powered BNN: accuracy at 8-sun equivalent vs bench supply
quote: Under an equivalent solar power of 8 suns, the circuit performs almost equivalently to when powered by a 1.2 volts lab bench supply.

claim: Solar-powered BNN: lowest illumination at which it still functions (with rising error)
quote: even under a very low equivalent solar power of 0.08 suns where the characteristics of the solar cell is strongly degraded, the circuit remains functional.
notes: Graceful degradation to approximate computing.

claim: Memristor BNN: measured energy per whole-chip inference (lab-bench supply, 0.7 V, 10 MHz)
quote: The lowest measured energy consumption of 45 nJ was achieved at a supply voltage of 0.7 volts
notes: Measured with bench supply, not while solar-powered. Simulated breakdown: MACs only 6.5% of energy, digital control dominates.

claim: Authors' reason for choosing digital near-memory rather than analog in-memory compute for a harvester-powered chip
quote: necessitating a stable and precise power supply, which is incompatible with the inherently unstable and unreliable energy harvesters.
notes: Direct counter-evidence for 'photovoltaic-driven ANALOG compute': analog MACs need regulated rails; only error-tolerant digital logic ran regulator-free.

claim: Photovoltaic silicon microring modulator (photocurrent self-charges the modulator; one transistor gates it): external electrical energy per bit
quote: show optical switching with an external electrical energy consumption as low as 20 zJ/bit at a data rate of 1 Mbps and an associated energy dissipation of 40 fJ/bit due to the photovoltaic effect.
notes: The light being modulated powers its own modulator: absorbed optical energy (40 fJ/bit) replaces the driver. Slow (1 Mbps). GlobalFoundries 45RFSOI, unmodified.

claim: Photovoltaic modulator: transistor voltage gain available without external electrical power (intrinsic gain gm*r0 in 45 nm)
quote: which is ≈15 in our 45 nm technology node as shown in the top plot of Fig. 3b.
notes: Self-biased by the photovoltaic charge; model/plot value.

claim: Photovoltaic modulator: SiGe-in-ring responsivity in unmodified GF 45RFSOI CMOS
quote: The SiGe ring is 300 nm wide and has partial overlap with the microring optical mode, resulting in a measured responsivity of R = 34 mA/W.
notes: Monolithic CMOS photonics; not a CORNERSTONE process.

claim: Self-powered (photovoltaic) perovskite sensor reservoir: 'near-zero' reservoir energy - the accounting excludes readout
quote: The energy is consumed only in the following processes, such as current-to-voltage conversion and weights programming in the readout memristor network.
notes: 'Zero' = device term in photovoltaic mode; I-V conversion and readout network are excluded by definition. 99.97% face classification (abstract).

claim: CORNERSTONE 220 nm SOI (passive/active) listed technology: etch depths, TiN heaters, 4 implants (active batches); no photodetector device listed
locator: Technology Platforms page, '220 nm silicon-on-insulator' technology details
quote: Technology details Si etch depths: 70 nm, 120 nm & 220 nm TiN based thermal phase shifters 4 implantation layers for active device batches
notes: Checked also: gdsfactory cspdk 1.4.5 si220 cells contain no photodetector/modulator cell (local .venv, 2026-09-27). Photodiodes only via bonded pick-and-place service (R4-043).

claim: CORNERSTONE 220 nm SOI active: carrier-depletion MZI modulator performance
value: >28 Gb/s, IL <5 dB, ER >3 dB @ 2 V
quote: Modulator performance (1.8 mm long MZI based carrier depletion): Speed @ 2 V dual drive: > 28 Gb/s
notes: 1.8 mm depletion MZMs: high capacitance vs microrings; no ring-modulator performance listed. Active run MPW #51 (R4-025).

claim: CORNERSTONE MPW #50 (220 nm SOI passive) adds a graphene integration beta service
locator: MPW Live Calls page, 'New for MPW #50: Graphene Integration'
quote: This MPW run will also introduce a new Graphene Integration Beta Service , delivered in partnership with the Cambridge Graphene Centre at the University of Cambridge .
notes: Device types (photodetector? modulator?) and performance are in the MPW #50 design rules, not read. Could enable on-chip detection on a passive run - unverified.

claim: DERIVED: ADC energy per MAC in the R3 N=128 crossbar if each detector integrates M = 100 cycles before one conversion (Netcast M)
quote: This energy is then divided by the number of MACs performed per integration window, which in the main text is M = 100.
notes: DERIVED: E_ADC / (N x M) = 2.19-15 pJ (R3-083/084) / (128 x 100). Assumes the accumulation dimension can be spread over time (TDM operands) and the slow ADC costs no more per conversion than a >=10 GS/s one (conservative).

claim: DERIVED: R3 bottom-up decode budget (accelerator + HBM, N=128, batch 64) with time-integrating receivers replacing TIA + per-cycle ADC
quote: As a result, the integrator and ADC can be M times slower, decreasing the cost of electrical readout components to ≈ (1/M ) pJ/MAC.
notes: DERIVED from R3-105: low 1.62 - 0.017 (ADC) - 0.019 (TIA) + 0.0002 = 1.58; high 1.80 - 0.117 - 0.019 + 0.0012 = 1.67 pJ/MAC. -2% to -8%: HBM weight streaming (1.46 pJ) untouched. x1.72 overhead -> 2.7-2.9 pJ/MAC.

claim: DERIVED: same substitution in prefill (weights reused over 2048 tokens)
quote: As a result, the integrator and ADC can be M times slower, decreasing the cost of electrical readout components to ≈ (1/M ) pJ/MAC.
notes: DERIVED from R3-106: 0.20 - 0.036 = 0.16; 0.39 - 0.135 = 0.26 pJ/MAC (-18% to -35%). vs B300 FP8 0.56 pJ/MAC chip (R3-070); still 5-bit detection.

claim: DERIVED: receiverless O-E-O activation amortised per MAC at N = 128 (30 fJ electrical + ~75 fJ optical per NOFU)
quote: over a carrier lifetime of ∼1 ns this corresponds to an energy consumption of 30 fJ per nonlinear operation (NLOP).
notes: DERIVED: 30 fJ / 128 = 0.23 fJ; 75 fJ / 128 = 0.59 fJ optical (R7-039). Replaces, per MAC: ADC 17-117 + TIA 19 + activation SRAM 38 + input DAC 3.9-7.8 fJ (R3-105 terms) = 78-182 fJ, but ONLY between layers whose weights are simultaneously resident on chip.

claim: DERIVED: R3 bottom-up budget with receiverless O-E-O layers (no ADC/TIA/SRAM/DAC between resident layers): decode / prefill
quote: Compared to prior approaches [14, 24], the NOFU directly drives the modulator through the photodiode and eliminates the amplifier stage between them.
notes: DERIVED from R3-105/106: decode 1.62-0.078+0.001 = 1.54; 1.80-0.182+0.001 = 1.62. Prefill 0.20-0.078 = 0.12; 0.39-0.182 = 0.21. Optimistic: assumes all layers resident (impossible for LLM weights; R3-012 PCM rewrite 67 uJ) and that the NOFU's tapped light needs no extra laser (it does: loss per layer, no gain).

claim: DERIVED: all-optical chi(2) activation amortised per MAC at N = 128 (16-80 fJ optical per activation)
quote: In this case, our device has an energy per activation of ∼ 16 fJ.
notes: DERIVED: 16 fJ (R7-058) or 80 fJ (R7-055) / 128. Excludes femtosecond pump/bias source wall-plug (not reported; bias 'can be reused' by assumption). Same arithmetic scale as the O-E-O NOFU, but speculative tier.

claim: DERIVED: NTT femtofarad O-E-O transistor energy amortised per MAC at N = 128
quote: Etotal = 21.5 ± 3.8 fJ/bit
notes: DERIVED: 21.5 fJ / 128 = 0.17 fJ/MAC. Caveat: measured for binary switching at 10 Gb/s, not an analog activation with 5-8 bit linearity; InP PhC platform.
